audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 2 Kings / Melakhim Bet Amaziah, Edom war, Israel-Judah conflict, assassination, Azariah, and Jeroboam II narrative, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for execution of regicides without descendant punishment, Edomite mass killing, royal challenge and parable, defeat and wall breach, temple plunder and hostages, assassination, adolescent coronation, imperial restoration, Jonah reference, affliction, and deliverance through a negatively evaluated king.

verses.restored: In second year of Joash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel, Amaziah son of Joash king of Judah became king.

familiar.text: In the second year of Joash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel reigned Amaziah the son of Joash king of Judah.

modern.text: In the second year of the reign of Jehoash son of Jehoahaz over Israel, Amaziah son of Joash became king of Judah.

original.text: בִּשְׁנַ֣ת שְׁתַּ֔יִם לְיוֹאָ֥שׁ בֶּן יוֹאָחָ֖ז מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל מָלַ֛ךְ אֲמַצְיָ֥הוּ בֶן יוֹאָ֖שׁ מֶ֥לֶךְ יְהוּדָֽה

verses.restored: Twenty-five years old was he when he became king, and twenty-nine years he reigned in Jerusalem. Name of his mother was Jehoaddan from Jerusalem.

familiar.text: He was twenty and five years old when he began to reign, and reigned twenty and nine years in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name was Jehoaddan of Jerusalem.

modern.text: He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem twenty-nine years. His mother’s name was Jehoaddan; she was from Jerusalem.

original.text: בֶּן עֶשְׂרִ֨ים וְחָמֵ֤שׁ שָׁנָה֙ הָיָ֣ה בְמָלְכ֔וֹ וְעֶשְׂרִ֤ים וָתֵ֨שַׁע֙ שָׁנָ֔ה מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְשֵׁ֣ם אִמּ֔וֹ יהועדין מִן יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם

verses.restored: He did what was right in eyes of YHWH, yet not like David his father; according to all Joash his father did, he did.

familiar.text: And he did that which was right in the sight of the LORD, yet not like David his father: he did according to all things as Joash his father did.

modern.text: And he did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, but not as his father David had done. He did everything as his father Joash had done.

original.text: וַיַּ֤עַשׂ הַיָּשָׁר֙ בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה רַ֕ק לֹ֖א כְּדָוִ֣ד אָבִ֑יו כְּכֹ֧ל אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂ֛ה יוֹאָ֥שׁ אָבִ֖יו עָשָֽׂה

verses.restored: Only high places were not removed; people were still sacrificing and burning incense at high places.

familiar.text: Howbeit the high places were not taken away: as yet the people did sacrifice and burnt incense on the high places.

modern.text: Nevertheless, the high places were not taken away, and the people continued sacrificing and burning incense on the high places.

original.text: רַ֥ק הַבָּמ֖וֹת לֹא סָ֑רוּ ע֥וֹד הָעָ֛ם מְזַבְּחִ֥ים וּֽמְקַטְּרִ֖ים בַּבָּמֽוֹת

verses.restored: When kingdom was strengthened in his hand, he struck his servants who had struck king his father.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, as soon as the kingdom was confirmed in his hand, that he slew his servants which had slain the king his father.

modern.text: As soon as the kingdom was firmly in his grasp, Amaziah executed the servants who had murdered his father the king.

original.text: וַיְהִ֕י כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר חָזְקָ֥ה הַמַּמְלָכָ֖ה בְּיָד֑וֹ וַיַּךְ֙ אֶת עֲבָדָ֔יו הַמַּכִּ֖ים אֶת הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ אָבִֽיו

verses.restored: But sons of those who struck him he did not put to death, according to what is written in scroll of Torah of Moses, which YHWH commanded, saying, Fathers shall not be put to death for sons, and sons shall not be put to death for fathers; each shall be put to death for his own sin.

familiar.text: But the children of the murderers he slew not: according unto that which is written in the book of the law of Moses, wherein the LORD commanded, saying, The fathers shall not be put to death for the children, nor the children be put to death for the fathers; but every man shall be put to death for his own sin.

modern.text: Yet he did not put the sons of the murderers to death, but acted according to what is written in the Book of the Law of Moses, where the LORD commanded: “Fathers must not be put to death for their children, and children must not be put to death for their fathers; each is to die for his own sin.”

original.text: וְאֶת בְּנֵ֥י הַמַּכִּ֖ים לֹ֣א הֵמִ֑ית כַּכָּת֣וּב בְּסֵ֣פֶר תּֽוֹרַת מֹ֠שֶׁה אֲשֶׁר צִוָּ֨ה יְהוָ֜ה לֵאמֹ֗ר לֹא יוּמְת֨וּ אָב֤וֹת עַל בָּנִים֙ וּבָנִים֙ לֹא יוּמְת֣וּ עַל אָב֔וֹת כִּ֛י אִם אִ֥ישׁ בְּחֶטְא֖וֹ ימות

verses.restored: He struck ten thousand of Edom in Valley of Salt and captured Sela in battle; he called its name Joktheel to this day.

familiar.text: He slew of Edom in the valley of salt ten thousand, and took Selah by war, and called the name of it Joktheel unto this day.

modern.text: Amaziah struck down 10,000 Edomites in the Valley of Salt. He took Sela in battle and called it Joktheel, which is its name to this very day. Jehoash Defeats Amaziah (2 Chronicles 25:17–24)

original.text: הוּא הִכָּ֨ה אֶת אֱד֤וֹם בְּגֵיא המלח עֲשֶׂ֣רֶת אֲלָפִ֔ים וְתָפַ֥שׂ אֶת הַסֶּ֖לַע בַּמִּלְחָמָ֑ה וַיִּקְרָ֤א אֶת שְׁמָהּ֙ יָקְתְאֵ֔ל עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה

verses.restored: Then Amaziah sent messengers to Jehoash son of Jehoahaz son of Jehu king of Israel, saying, Come, let us see one another face to face.

familiar.text: Then Amaziah sent messengers to Jehoash, the son of Jehoahaz son of Jehu, king of Israel, saying, Come, let us look one another in the face.

modern.text: Then Amaziah sent messengers to the king of Israel Jehoash son of Jehoahaz, the son of Jehu. “Come, let us meet face to face,” he said.

original.text: אָ֣ז שָׁלַ֤ח אֲמַצְיָה֙ מַלְאָכִ֔ים אֶל יְהוֹאָ֨שׁ בֶּן יְהוֹאָחָ֧ז בֶּן יֵה֛וּא מֶ֥לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר לְכָ֖ה נִתְרָאֶ֥ה פָנִֽים

verses.restored: Jehoash king of Israel sent to Amaziah king of Judah, saying, The thornbush in Lebanon sent to cedar in Lebanon, saying, Give your daughter to my son as wife. But a wild animal in Lebanon passed and trampled thornbush.

familiar.text: And Jehoash the king of Israel sent to Amaziah king of Judah, saying, The thistle that was in Lebanon sent to the cedar that was in Lebanon, saying, Give thy daughter to my son to wife: and there passed by a wild beast that was in Lebanon, and trode down the thistle.

modern.text: But Jehoash king of Israel replied to Amaziah king of Judah: “A thistle in Lebanon sent a message to a cedar in Lebanon, saying, ‘Give your daughter to my son in marriage.’ Then a wild beast in Lebanon came along and trampled the thistle.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֞ח יְהוֹאָ֣שׁ מֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אֶל אֲמַצְיָ֣הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָה֮ לֵאמֹר֒ הַח֜וֹחַ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּלְּבָנ֗וֹן שָׁ֠לַח אֶל הָאֶ֜רֶז אֲשֶׁ֤ר בַּלְּבָנוֹן֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר תְּנָֽה אֶת בִּתְּךָ֥ לִבְנִ֖י לְאִשָּׁ֑ה וַֽתַּעֲבֹ֞ר חַיַּ֤ת הַשָּׂדֶה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּלְּבָנ֔וֹן וַתִּרְמֹ֖ס אֶת הַחֽוֹחַ

verses.restored: Striking, you have struck Edom, and your heart has lifted you. Be honored and stay in your house. Why stir yourself into harm, so you fall, you and Judah with you?

familiar.text: Thou hast indeed smitten Edom, and thine heart hath lifted thee up: glory of this, and tarry at home: for why shouldest thou meddle to thy hurt, that thou shouldest fall, even thou, and Judah with thee?

modern.text: You have indeed defeated Edom, and your heart has become proud. Glory in that and stay at home. Why should you stir up trouble so that you fall—you and Judah with you?”

original.text: הַכֵּ֤ה הִכִּ֨יתָ֙ אֶת אֱד֔וֹם וּֽנְשָׂאֲךָ֖ לִבֶּ֑ךָ הִכָּבֵד֙ וְשֵׁ֣ב בְּבֵיתֶ֔ךָ וְלָ֤מָּה תִתְגָּרֶה֙ בְּרָעָ֔ה וְנָ֣פַלְתָּ֔ה אַתָּ֖ה וִיהוּדָ֥ה עִמָּֽךְ

verses.restored: But Amaziah did not listen. Jehoash king of Israel went up, and he and Amaziah king of Judah saw one another face to face at Beth-shemesh, which belongs to Judah.

familiar.text: But Amaziah would not hear. Therefore Jehoash king of Israel went up; and he and Amaziah king of Judah looked one another in the face at Bethshemesh, which belongeth to Judah.

modern.text: But Amaziah would not listen, and Jehoash king of Israel advanced. He and King Amaziah of Judah faced each other at Beth-shemesh in Judah.

original.text: וְלֹא שָׁמַ֣ע אֲמַצְיָ֔הוּ וַיַּ֨עַל יְהוֹאָ֤שׁ מֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וַיִּתְרָא֣וּ פָנִ֔ים ה֖וּא וַאֲמַצְיָ֣הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה בְּבֵ֥ית שֶׁ֖מֶשׁ אֲשֶׁ֥ר לִיהוּדָֽה

verses.restored: Judah was struck before Israel, and each fled to his tent.

familiar.text: And Judah was put to the worse before Israel; and they fled every man to their tents.

modern.text: And Judah was routed before Israel, and every man fled to his home.

original.text: וַיִּנָּ֥גֶף יְהוּדָ֖ה לִפְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיָּנֻ֖סוּ אִ֥ישׁ לאהלו

verses.restored: Jehoash king of Israel seized Amaziah king of Judah, son of Jehoash son of Ahaziah, at Beth-shemesh. He came to Jerusalem and broke wall of Jerusalem from Ephraim Gate to Corner Gate, four hundred cubits.

familiar.text: And Jehoash king of Israel took Amaziah king of Judah, the son of Jehoash the son of Ahaziah, at Bethshemesh, and came to Jerusalem, and brake down the wall of Jerusalem from the gate of Ephraim unto the corner gate, four hundred cubits.

modern.text: There at Beth-shemesh, Jehoash king of Israel captured Amaziah king of Judah, the son of Joash, the son of Ahaziah. Then Jehoash went to Jerusalem and broke down the wall of Jerusalem from the Ephraim Gate to the Corner Gate—a section of four hundred cubits.

original.text: וְאֵת֩ אֲמַצְיָ֨הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָ֜ה בֶּן יְהוֹאָ֣שׁ בֶּן אֲחַזְיָ֗הוּ תָּפַ֛שׂ יְהוֹאָ֥שׁ מֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּבֵ֣ית שָׁ֑מֶשׁ ויבאו יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וַיִּפְרֹץ֩ בְּחוֹמַ֨ת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֜ם בְּשַׁ֤עַר אֶפְרַ֨יִם֙ עַד שַׁ֣עַר הַפִּנָּ֔ה אַרְבַּ֥ע מֵא֖וֹת אַמָּֽה

verses.restored: He took all gold and silver, all vessels found in house of YHWH and treasuries of king's house, and hostages, and returned to Samaria.

familiar.text: And he took all the gold and silver, and all the vessels that were found in the house of the LORD, and in the treasures of the king’s house, and hostages, and returned to Samaria.

modern.text: He took all the gold and silver and all the articles found in the house of the LORD and in the treasuries of the royal palace, as well as some hostages. Then he returned to Samaria. Jeroboam II Succeeds Jehoash in Israel

original.text: וְלָקַ֣ח אֶת כָּל הַזָּהָב וְ֠הַכֶּסֶף וְאֵ֨ת כָּל הַכֵּלִ֜ים הַנִּמְצְאִ֣ים בֵּית יְהוָ֗ה וּבְאֹֽצְרוֹת֙ בֵּ֣ית הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְאֵ֖ת בְּנֵ֣י הַתַּֽעֲרֻב֑וֹת וַיָּ֖שָׁב שֹׁמְרֽוֹנָה

verses.restored: Remaining acts of Jehoash, what he did, his might, and how he fought Amaziah king of Judah, are they not written in scroll of matters of days of kings of Israel?

familiar.text: Now the rest of the acts of Jehoash which he did, and his might, and how he fought with Amaziah king of Judah, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?

modern.text: As for the rest of the acts of Jehoash, along with his accomplishments, his might, and how he waged war against Amaziah king of Judah, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?

original.text: וְיֶתֶר֩ דִּבְרֵ֨י יְהוֹאָ֜שׁ אֲשֶׁ֤ר עָשָׂה֙ וּגְב֣וּרָת֔וֹ וַאֲשֶׁ֣ר נִלְחַ֔ם עִ֖ם אֲמַצְיָ֣הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה הֲלֹא הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַיָּמִ֖ים לְמַלְכֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: Jehoash lay with his fathers and was buried in Samaria with kings of Israel. Jeroboam his son became king in his place.

familiar.text: And Jehoash slept with his fathers, and was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel; and Jeroboam his son reigned in his stead.

modern.text: And Jehoash rested with his fathers and was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel. And his son Jeroboam reigned in his place. The Death of Amaziah (2 Chronicles 25:25–28)

original.text: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֤ב יְהוֹאָשׁ֙ עִם אֲבֹתָ֔יו וַיִּקָּבֵר֙ בְּשֹׁ֣מְר֔וֹן עִ֖ם מַלְכֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ יָרָבְעָ֥ם בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו

verses.restored: Amaziah son of Joash king of Judah lived fifteen years after death of Jehoash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel.

familiar.text: And Amaziah the son of Joash king of Judah lived after the death of Jehoash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel fifteen years.

modern.text: Amaziah son of Joash king of Judah lived for fifteen years after the death of Joash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel.

original.text: וַיְחִ֨י אֲמַצְיָ֤הוּ בֶן יוֹאָשׁ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה אַֽחֲרֵ֣י מ֔וֹת יְהוֹאָ֥שׁ בֶּן יְהֽוֹאָחָ֖ז מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל חֲמֵ֥שׁ עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה שָׁנָֽה

verses.restored: Remaining acts of Amaziah, are they not written in scroll of matters of days of kings of Judah?

familiar.text: And the rest of the acts of Amaziah, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?

modern.text: As for the rest of the acts of Amaziah, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?

original.text: וְיֶ֖תֶר דִּבְרֵ֣י אֲמַצְיָ֑הוּ הֲלֹא הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַיָּמִ֖ים לְמַלְכֵ֥י יְהוּדָֽה

verses.restored: They conspired against him in Jerusalem. He fled to Lachish, but they sent after him to Lachish and put him to death there.

familiar.text: Now they made a conspiracy against him in Jerusalem: and he fled to Lachish; but they sent after him to Lachish, and slew him there.

modern.text: And conspirators plotted against Amaziah in Jerusalem, and he fled to Lachish. But men were sent after him to Lachish, and they killed him there.

original.text: וַיִּקְשְׁר֨וּ עָלָ֥יו קֶ֛שֶׁר בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם וַיָּ֣נָס לָכִ֑ישָׁה וַיִּשְׁלְח֤וּ אַֽחֲרָיו֙ לָכִ֔ישָׁה וַיְמִתֻ֖הוּ שָֽׁם

verses.restored: They carried him on horses, and he was buried in Jerusalem with his fathers in city of David.

familiar.text: And they brought him on horses: and he was buried at Jerusalem with his fathers in the city of David.

modern.text: They carried him back on horses and buried him in Jerusalem with his fathers in the City of David. Azariah Succeeds Amaziah in Judah (2 Chronicles 26:1–2)

original.text: וַיִּשְׂא֥וּ אֹת֖וֹ עַל הַסּוּסִ֑ים וַיִּקָּבֵ֧ר בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֛ם עִם אֲבֹתָ֖יו בְּעִ֥יר דָּוִֽד

verses.restored: All people of Judah took Azariah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in place of his father Amaziah.

familiar.text: And all the people of Judah took Azariah, which was sixteen years old, and made him king instead of his father Amaziah.

modern.text: Then all the people of Judah took Azariah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in place of his father Amaziah.

original.text: וַיִּקְח֞וּ כָּל עַ֤ם יְהוּדָה֙ אֶת עֲזַרְיָ֔ה וְה֕וּא בֶּן שֵׁ֥שׁ עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה שָׁנָ֑ה וַיַּמְלִ֣כוּ אֹת֔וֹ תַּ֖חַת אָבִ֥יו אֲמַצְיָֽהוּ

verses.restored: He built Elath and restored it to Judah after king lay with his fathers.

familiar.text: He built Elath, and restored it to Judah, after that the king slept with his fathers.

modern.text: Azariah was the one who rebuilt Elath and restored it to Judah after King Amaziah rested with his fathers. Jeroboam II Reigns in Israel

original.text: ה֚וּא בָּנָ֣ה אֶת אֵילַ֔ת וַיְשִׁבֶ֖הָ לִֽיהוּדָ֑ה אַחֲרֵ֥י שְׁכַֽב הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ עִם אֲבֹתָֽיו

verses.restored: In fifteenth year of Amaziah son of Joash king of Judah, Jeroboam son of Joash king of Israel became king in Samaria and reigned forty-one years.

familiar.text: In the fifteenth year of Amaziah the son of Joash king of Judah Jeroboam the son of Joash king of Israel began to reign in Samaria, and reigned forty and one years.

modern.text: In the fifteenth year of the reign of Amaziah son of Joash over Judah, Jeroboam son of Jehoash became king of Israel, and he reigned in Samaria forty-one years.

original.text: בִּשְׁנַת֙ חֲמֵשׁ עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֔ה לַאֲמַצְיָ֥הוּ בֶן יוֹאָ֖שׁ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה מָ֠לַךְ יָרָבְעָ֨ם בֶּן יוֹאָ֤שׁ מֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בְּשֹׁ֣מְר֔וֹן אַרְבָּעִ֥ים וְאַחַ֖ת שָׁנָֽה

verses.restored: He did evil in eyes of YHWH; he did not turn from all sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin.

familiar.text: And he did that which was evil in the sight of the LORD: he departed not from all the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin.

modern.text: And he did evil in the sight of the LORD and did not turn away from all the sins that Jeroboam son of Nebat had caused Israel to commit.

original.text: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה לֹ֣א סָ֗ר מִכָּל חַטֹּאות֙ יָרָבְעָ֣ם בֶּן נְבָ֔ט אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶחֱטִ֖יא אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: He restored border of Israel from entrance of Hamath to sea of Arabah, according to word of YHWH, Divine of Israel, spoken through his servant Jonah son of Amittai, prophet from Gath-hepher.

familiar.text: He restored the coast of Israel from the entering of Hamath unto the sea of the plain, according to the word of the LORD God of Israel, which he spake by the hand of his servant Jonah, the son of Amittai, the prophet, which was of Gathhepher.

modern.text: This Jeroboam restored the boundary of Israel from Lebo-hamath to the Sea of the Arabah, according to the word that the LORD, the God of Israel, had spoken through His servant Jonah son of Amittai, the prophet from Gath-hepher.

verses.restored: Remaining acts of Jeroboam, all he did, his might, how he fought, and how he restored Damascus and Hamath to Judah/Israel, are they not written in scroll of matters of days of kings of Israel?

familiar.text: Now the rest of the acts of Jeroboam, and all that he did, and his might, how he warred, and how he recovered Damascus, and Hamath, which belonged to Judah, for Israel, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?

modern.text: As for the rest of the acts of Jeroboam, along with all his accomplishments and might, and how he waged war and recovered both Damascus and Hamath for Israel from Judah, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?

translation_notes: Verse 6 explicitly rejects inherited criminal punishment. It is a major safeguard against executing children for parents, collective family guilt, blood-feud logic, and political purges.
Amaziah's execution of his father's killers is still capital punishment under royal power; the restraint toward their children does not automatically validate the executions themselves.
The killing of ten thousand Edomites and seizure/renaming of Sela are conquest violence. Edomites are not a timeless enemy, and modern territorial claims cannot be built from this account.
The thornbush-and-cedar parable challenges royal pride but uses a marriage proposal as political imagery. Daughters are not diplomatic property.
Amaziah rejects warning and brings defeat, wall destruction, plunder, and hostages upon others. A leader's pride imposes costs on people who did not choose the challenge.
Hostages are human beings under coercion, not inventory beside temple treasure.
Amaziah's assassination lacks narrated due process. His earlier legal restraint does not protect him from the same political violence that killed his father.
Azariah is made king at sixteen; adolescence must not be romanticized as readiness for unaccountable rule.
Jeroboam II receives a negative moral evaluation yet becomes an instrument of relief because the people's suffering is seen. Help is not proof that a ruler or regime is righteous.
Border restoration and references to Damascus/Hamath require historical, textual, and geopolitical audit and cannot ground modern expansionism.
safety_note: Center the chapter's rejection of inherited punishment while refusing to glorify executions, Edomite mass killing, conquest, hostages, adolescent kingship, assassination, or territorial expansion. A ruler's pride can expose an entire population to consequences, and relief for suffering people does not sanctify the ruler through whom it comes.
